statement: The monodromy of the eight ordinary circles tangent to three labelled general circles is the inner holomorph D₈ ⋊ Inn(D₈), where D₈ denotes the dihedral group of order 8. It has order 32 and GAP identifier SmallGroup(32,49).

answer.qualification: The exact group description is displayed in Zeng’s notes, using the singular-curve theta-characteristic framework attributed there to Harris (1982). Direct confirmation that Harris states this exact Apollonius group remains unavailable. The action uses ordinary circle coefficients without adjoining chosen square roots of squared radii.

source.location: Author lecture notes, Harris 1982 singular-curve theta-characteristic section and subsequent Apollonian-circle group calculation (inner holomorph and GAP 32,49).
source.version: Author-hosted 2025 notes; original Harris article remains unavailable for direct inspection.

scope: Labelled input circles parameterized by their ordinary conic coefficients, without adjoining chosen square roots of their squared radii.
notes:
Zeng’s notes display the inner-holomorph description and identification SmallGroup(32,49), and credit Harris (1982) for the singular-curve theta-characteristic framework. This pass does not establish that the exact Apollonius group is stated in Harris, whose article could not be inspected. The stored permutations give a transitive realization of the displayed group; their labels are abstract solution labels. Do not confuse this action with McKean’s set-theoretic (C₂)^3 duality action or the group after base change to chosen radii. The LMFDB link identifies the recorded degree-eight permutation group.

Related literature. Theta-characteristics on algebraic curves (Joe Harris, 1982). Historical or related contributions are retained here. Their own precise statements have not been independently verified for a separate result in this migration.
